summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — FICO +10%, MDT +4%, META +3%, ZBH +3%, PODD +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CIEN -10%, LITE -10%, COHR -7%, BE -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CIEN (-10.37%) — No company-specific news found. CIEN fell with a broad AI-optical selloff (LITE, COHR, GLW also down ~6-10%), likely profit-taking and de-risking of crowded high-beta names. Sources dated the drop Oct 12, so the date is unconfirmed. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: CIEN is a ~$57B mid/large-cap optical-networking name that no strategy includes. It also has no earnings catalyst for a news-reactive bot, and a long-only bot would not short a sector-wide momentum unwind.

top_movers.catalyst: Oversold rebound after the ~22% FHFA/VantageScore mortgage-scoring selloff; support came from UWM sticking with FICO scores and analysts keeping Buy ratings (Money Morning, 10/13).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FICO is a mid/large-cap software and analytics name that no strategy lists. It was also a headline-driven rebound after a crash, so momentum and gap filters would likely have rejected it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'post-crash rebound' scan to the universe builder: admit any S&P 500 name that fell ≥15% within 10 days and then gaps up ≥5% on volume ≥2× its 20-day average, as a candidate list for the news-reactive strategy.

top_movers.suggestion: Add mega-cap tech names such as META to the momentum universe, and add a 2-day cumulative-return trigger (≥ +6% with an analyst PT upgrade) that doesn't need a single-session gap or volume spike.
